topics.h1: The Fathers, by the questions they answered.
topics.intro: A doctrinal index for enquirers, catechumens, and lay apologists. Pick a topic and read what the Fathers confessed, with each citation linking straight to the work it is drawn from.
topics.emptyState: No curated topics yet. The first entries are landing as the editorial team writes them; check back soon.
discover.subtitle: Saints, councils, the calendar, and a way into the wider library.
discover.mobileSubtitle: The whole library at a glance.
discover.tile.historyBlurb: Two thousand years on one timeline: the councils, schisms, saints, and missions, every event sourced.
discover.tile.saintsBlurb: The lives of the saints, with their works to read in full.
discover.tile.councilsBlurb: The seven Ecumenical Councils and the synods before Nicaea, in their own words.
discover.tile.theologyBlurb: The long-form study of doctrine, the mind of the Fathers set out in essay form.
discover.tile.apologeticsBlurb: The defence of the Faith, the Orthodox answer to disputed questions of doctrine and history.
discover.tile.readingBlurb: The long Fathers, read at length, with the page where you left off remembered.
discover.tile.calendarBlurb: Every day of the Church's year, the fasts, and the count to Pascha.
discover.tile.dailyReadingsBlurb: The appointed Epistle and Gospel for today.
discover.tile.psalterBlurb: The hundred fifty psalms, in the Septuagint numbering.
discover.tile.patristicBlurb: The Fathers verse by verse, beside the text of Scripture.
discover.tile.topicsBlurb: One thread, traced across the Fathers, side by side.
discover.tile.heresiesBlurb: The errors the councils condemned, defined and answered by the Fathers.
reading.subtitle: Sit down with the Fathers. Continue where you left off, see what others return to, and find where to read next.
reading.surface.patristicBlurb: The Fathers in full, translated and free to read.
reading.surface.saintsBlurb: Each life, with the works left to us in their own hand.
reading.surface.councilsBlurb: The creeds, canons, and definitions the Church confessed.
reading.surface.topicsBlurb: One thread, traced across the Fathers, side by side.
reading.surface.collectionsBlurb: Florilegia, the witnesses of the Fathers gathered on one theme.
calendar.h1: Every day of the Church's year.
prayers.today.noSaint: No saint indexed for this day
prayers.today.morningBlurb: Sign of the Cross, O Heavenly King, the Trisagion, the Lord's Prayer, Rising from Sleep, the Jesus Prayer, the Theotokos hymn, and the dismissal. About 8 minutes.
prayers.today.eveningBlurb: The Trisagion, the Lord's Prayer, a brief examination of the day, the Jesus Prayer, Into Thy hands, and the dismissal. About 8 minutes.
prayers.today.jesusPrayerText: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
prayers.today.jesusPrayerBlurb: Pray it in the breath, with the heart, at any time. The monastics call it the prayer of the heart; the Fathers say the bringing-back is half the work.
prayers.today.ropeBlurb: Count the Jesus Prayer on a digital komvoschini. 33, 50, or 100 knots. Quiet by default.
prayers.epitaphMessage: There are no streaks here. The rule is the rule; the day is the day. Pick it up whenever.
prayers.push.label: Prayer reminders
prayers.push.body: One nudge in the morning, one in the evening. Off by default.

pwa.install.modal.title: Install Purify on your computer
pwa.install.modal.firefox: Firefox doesn't yet support installing Purify directly. Open this page in Chrome, Edge, Brave, or Arc and tap Download Purify again.
pwa.install.modal.safari17: Click the Share button in Safari's toolbar, then choose Add to Dock. Purify will install with its own icon and window.
pwa.install.modal.safariOld: Your Safari version doesn't support adding Purify to the Dock. Update macOS to Sonoma or later, or open this page in Chrome, Edge, or Brave to install.
pwa.install.modal.chromiumSuppressed: Purify may already be installed, or your browser paused the install prompt. Open it from your Applications or Start menu.
pwa.install.modal.ipad: On iPad, tap the Share button in Safari's toolbar, then choose Add to Home Screen.
onboard.welcome.title: A quiet place to pray, read, and keep the Church's year.
onboard.welcome.body: The saint of the day, the fast, the appointed readings, and the prayers, gathered into one calm place. No account needed to begin.
onboard.personalize.calendarBody: This sets the saints and fasts you'll see each day. You can change it any time in Settings.
onboard.personalize.calNewSub: Most Greek, Antiochian, and Romanian parishes
onboard.personalize.calOldSub: Russian, Serbian, and Old-Calendar parishes, 13 days behind
onboard.personalize.focusBody: Choose any. We'll point you to a good first step, nothing is locked away.
onboard.reminders.title: A nudge to pray, morning and evening.
onboard.reminders.body: One gentle reminder in the morning, one in the evening. Off whenever you like. They run through your device's own notifications, with no third-party tracker.
onboard.reminders.blocked: Notifications are blocked in your browser settings. You can turn them on later from the You tab.
onboard.reminders.unsupported: This device doesn't support reminders, but everything else works.
onboard.account.title: Carry your prayers on every device.
onboard.account.body: A free account keeps your bookmarks, highlights, and reading place safe, and follows you to any device you sign in on. Purify works fully without one.
